label: Home Battery Start v4.15.1
info:
# Awaited write section (demo for issue #171)

Copy of the Start flow. Node ids match the original, so this REPLACES the
Start flow tab. Do not import it next to the original; diff it against
`node-red/01 start-flow.json`.

## Starting point

HA's `ModbusHub` holds one `asyncio.Lock()` **per hub**, and Fonske defines one
hub per battery. So:

- two writes to the same battery were already serial (HA does that itself);
- writes to different batteries really run in parallel over separate TCP
  connections.

Serializing everything would make the cycle N times longer. This version is
serial per battery and parallel across batteries.

## What changed

1. **Write gate** in front of `Timing start`: one cycle at a time. A tick
   during a running cycle is coalesced (one slot, newest wins), not dropped.
2. **The loop stays fast.** `Set Batteries` steps on immediately, so every
   battery is put to work right after the previous one.
3. **Serial chain per battery**: `Set mode (awaited)` -> `Power write?` ->
   `Set power (awaited)`. The power write only leaves once HA finished the mode
   write, so HBC keeps at most 1 outstanding request per hub.
4. **RBE replaced** by an explicit comparison. A filter node in a serial chain
   is a dead end: if it blocks, that battery never reports to the collector.
5. **Collector** waits until every battery reported (done, skipped or failed)
   and then releases the lock through `Write done`.
6. **Error handling**: a `catch` on both call nodes reports the battery anyway,
   plus a stale-lock failsafe in `Write gate`.
7. **Write done** measures the real wall clock of the cycle and sets
   `flow.write_execution_time`, which `Operational thresholds` now uses.

## Cost

Wiring the call outputs costs no extra websocket traffic: the node already does
`await websocket.callService(...)` before it calls `send()`, so that round trip
happened anyway. The only added latency is one round trip between the mode and
power write of the same battery (a few ms plus one
`message_wait_milliseconds`), and it does not add up across batteries.

## Layout

Three groups, readable left to right:

- **Set Batteries** (left column): entry, `Write gate`, `Timing start`,
  `Loop start`. Deliberately left of the Loop group.
- **Loop**: the write chain, the dispatch row, the loop row, and on the right
  the join point `Collect completions`. The error branch sits just left of the
  collector to keep that wire short.
- **Write completion (await)** (bottom right): `Timing end` -> `Write done` ->
  `Done`. On the right so `Write done` sits next to the debug dashboard group
  it writes to.

Nodes that belong together share an x. Columns: 230 entry, 430 loop driver,
630 mode, 830 power decision, 1030 power write, 1120 collector.

The feedback for a coalesced cycle runs through the link pair
`rerun coalesced` -> `rerun`. As a wire it became a ~1400px diagonal straight
through the section. Select either link node and Node-RED highlights its peer.

Careful when moving nodes: the group **Update UI: debug dashboard** covers
x 1234..1866, y 1479..1681. Everything in this section must stay left of or
below that, or a node ends up in the wrong group.
